problem: Appearance-driven residency cleanup can release image A while an offscreen object's bind group still references it. Reloading A under the same URL previously reused the old bind group and sampled the destroyed generation. Label collection has the same lifetime boundary.

beforeProof.method: Actual WebGPURenderer.object() from the built Engine with fake GPU texture identities

fix.behavior: Record and compare actual albedo, normal, ORM, height and label texture identities in both needsPrepare() and object() before reusing a GPU bind group.
fix.scope: Geometry, shader math, material values and texture residency policy remain unchanged.

regression.scenario: Full renderer transaction: visible A, move outside all views, patch to B and collect, patch back to A and reload, return to the visible scene.
checks: The offscreen object retains its old binding while all A images and label are evicted.
Reentry replaces the bind group with the new image and label generations.
A draw fails the fake GPU check if any bound image or label has been destroyed.
Each image channel also refreshes when the URL, material identity and pose remain unchanged.
A removed label generation refreshes under the same text and color key.

validation.nativeGpuRun: The extended native render stability harness subsequently passed on AMD RDNA-3 with zero validation errors. The A-to-B-to-A binding-lifetime regression itself executes production renderer methods against a resource-lifetime-checking fake GPU.
